sentences.text: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025, a 7.3% CAGR [D5][D206].
The path was a step change, not a compounder: revenue was $120 billion in FY2020 and $129 billion in FY2022 before jumping 22.9% in FY2023 to $158 billion [D86][D134][D159][D179].
That FY2023 step came from net interest income, up 33.8% to $89.3 billion, with interest income at $171 billion [F8][D174][X125].
FY2025 growth slowed to 2.8%, with net interest income up 3.1% and noninterest income up 2.4% [D226][D221][D222].
Net interest income compounded at 8.4% over the window against 6.2% for noninterest income, so the spread business carried the growth [F111][F112].
North America remains the concentration, at 76.6% of revenue in FY2025, but contributed only 0.2pp of the year's growth [D249][D251].
Asia-Pacific grew 17.3% and EMEA 9.5%, contributing 1.2pp each [D300][D301][D275][D276].

FY2025 net interest income growth came from higher Markets net interest income, higher Card Services revolving balances and higher wholesale deposit balances, largely offset by deposit margin compression [P28].
Net income fell 2.6% to $57.0 billion while diluted EPS rose 1.4% to $20.02, as the diluted share count fell 3.4% [F30][D214][F50][D216][D224].
The efficiency ratio was 52.4% in FY2025, better than the 57.2% window median and near the 51.7% window low set in FY2024 [D207][D333][D331].
That is 9.3pp below the 61.7% peer median and the best of the seven banks in the group [D207][D337][D336].
Noninterest expense rose 4.2% to $95.6 billion, driven by higher compensation, brokerage and distribution fees, auto lease depreciation, technology and marketing [D225][X137][P26].
The credit-loss provision rose to 7.8% of revenue from 6.0%, above the 6.0% peer median [D208][D185][D341].
Net margin held at 31.2% against 32.9% in FY2024, with the effective tax rate at 21.4% versus 22.1% [D210][D187][D203][D180].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank; it was negative $148 billion in FY2025 against $57.0 billion of net income [F60][F30].
The outflow came from higher trading assets, higher securities borrowed, net loan originations and higher other assets, partly offset by net income [P21].
Capital return is the better test: buybacks plus dividends of $48.2 billion were 85% of net income in FY2025, up from $33.6 billion in FY2024 [D205][F30][D182].
Total assets grew 10.5% to $4.42 trillion in FY2025, with loans up to $1.47 trillion and deposits to $2.56 trillion [F90][D218][X197][X207].
Loans were 57.3% of deposits, up from 55.0%, still well below the 64.7% of FY2016 [D211][D188][D10].
Return on average equity was 16.1%, against an 11.8% peer median and the top of the seven-bank group [D213][D339][D338].
The firm repurchased $31.6 billion of stock and paid $16.6 billion of dividends in FY2025, cutting the diluted share count 3.4% [X102][X112][D224].
Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy's pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, and differs by up to 0.10% [R1][F30][X20].
The gap is small but it means FY2025 net income of $57.0 billion should be read as $57.0 billion per the 10-K [F30][X20].
Criticized wholesale exposure rose to $48.5 billion from $44.7 billion, driven by SPEs, Consumer & Retail, Banks & Finance Companies, Healthcare and Chemicals & Plastics [P2].
The FY2020 pretax income and tax figures were later restated, and the pack uses the first-reported values [R2][R3][X63][X73].
If the efficiency ratio moves back above the 57.2% window median, the cost advantage described above would be reversing [D333].
A credit-loss provision above the FY2025 level of 7.8% of revenue would confirm the criticized-exposure build is reaching the income statement [D208].
Net interest income growth below the FY2025 3.1% would signal that deposit margin compression is outrunning loan growth [D221].
